essence: Bhairava is established as all-pervading conscious reality: one, endless, beginningless — the Absolute that pervades moving and unmoving states.
The Lord is then venerated as refuge of the helpless by a mind become His — veneration as mental absorption, not ritual offering.
The nirukta of Bhairava (bearing/supporting, the Roar of AHAM, benefactor of the terrified) is here performed, not stated: the name is lived.
Total surrender is sized to its object — the all-pervading consciousness is venerated by absorption into it.

sections.SUMMARY: The Lord is established as all-pervading conscious reality — one, endless, beginningless — then venerated as refuge of the helpless by a mind become His.

rasa.sthayibhava: śānta (tranquility) as veneration of all-pervading consciousness
rasa.justification: The sthāyibhāva is devotion (bhakti) in the mode of veneration (vandana); the vyabhicāri is wonder (camatkāra) at consciousness pervading all. The rasa is not erotic or heroic but the tranquility of recognition beginning: the Absolute named, the devotee absorbed. Abhinava's own rasa theory (rasadhvani) is here the frame, not decoration — the verse aims at relish (camatkāra) of the Absolute, and the C1 names that relish.
